learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of continuous integration and continuous delivery.
Identify the stages of a Java application delivery pipeline.
Design a basic CI/CD workflow for testing and deploying a Java application.

activities.title: CI/CD Pipeline Map
activities.instruction: Connect the stages of the delivery pipeline.

content.concept: A CI/CD pipeline automates activities such as source validation, building, testing, packaging, and deployment.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Pipeline Sequencer
activities.instruction: Arrange the CI/CD stages in order.

content.concept: A typical Java pipeline checks out code, resolves dependencies, builds the project, runs tests, packages the application, and deploys it.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Quality Gate Selector
activities.instruction: Select the correct pipeline quality gate.

content.concept: Automated tests and quality checks can prevent a build from progressing when required conditions are not satisfied.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: CI/CD Builder
activities.instruction: Build a complete Java delivery pipeline.

content.concept: A CI/CD workflow combines source control, automated builds, tests, artifacts, and deployment into a repeatable delivery process.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
